content: age/ssh-to-age key management (HIGH ssh-to-age README + agenix README): ssh-to-age deterministically derives X25519 age key from ed25519 SSH key (birational map); cannot recover SSH key from age key; age key does not grant SSH auth. A passphrase-protected SSH key derived to an UNENCRYPTED age key file means anyone with the file decrypts every secret - the passphrase protection is bypassed for decryption; use age-plugin-yubikey/TPM or encrypted volume if you need at-rest protection. Losing the private identity = permanent loss (age has no recovery); keep an admin/recovery key (backed up offline) in every creation_rule as escape hatch (HALLway/unmovedcentre pattern). sops -r rotates only the data key, NOT recipients - use sops updatekeys to add/remove recipients and re-encrypt. age is NOT post-quantum safe: repo-committed ciphertext enables harvest-now-decrypt-later (FiloSottile/age#578, agenix README); extra-sensitive secrets should be rotated periodically. SSH key rotation invalidates all age keys derived from it - rekey when rotating SSH keys.
